query: Consider the following context: Constituent phases and their corresponding phase transformations are important in developing alloys. In that context, which method can be used for control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Controlled thermal annealing in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys can modulate phase evolution by favoring a balanced development of ductile FCC and strengthening BCC phases while suppressing the formation of brittle, ordered phases.
generation.material_initial_state: Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloy initially produced via rapid solidification or conventional melting, exhibiting a mixture of metastable phases.
generation.intervention: A thermal annealing treatment with precisely controlled temperature and time profiles.
generation.conditions: Annealing experiments conducted under varying temperatures and durations, optionally followed by controlled cooling schedules to adjust atomic diffusion kinetics.
generation.structural_mediator: Relative phase fractions, particularly the stabilization of FCC and BCC phases and reduction of brittle ordered phases such as B2.
generation.mechanism: Annealing enables atomic diffusion that drives phase transformations, where specific temperature-time regimes can kinetically favor the formation of desired ductile and strengthening phases while inhibiting phases that compromise mechanical integrity.
generation.predicted_outcome: A microstructure with enhanced phase uniformity, showing an optimal balance between ductile FCC and strengthening BCC phases, resulting in improved mechanical properties over the untreated baseline.
generation.baseline: The alloy produced without controlled annealing, which typically exhibits a less desirable phase mixture including unwanted brittle phases.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies within controlled thermal processing regimes for the Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni system and may not extend to conditions that cause excessive grain growth or full homogenization beyond the targeted phase balance.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative effects of specific annealing parameters on phase fractions and mechanical properties remain uncertain, necessitating detailed experiments to optimize the heat treatment schedule.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare multiple samples of the Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy and subject them to a series of annealing treatments with systematically varied temperatures and durations, alongside a control group with no annealing.
measurements: Microstructural characterization using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) or transmission electron microscopy (TEM)
Mechanical properties evaluation via tensile or hardness testing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If controlled annealing does not result in a statistically significant increase in the proportion of FCC and BCC phases, or fails to improve the mechanical properties compared to the untreated control, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

recalled_precedents.approach: They performed systematic annealing experiments on Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high‐entropy alloys to control phase evolution. By varying annealing temperatures and times, they modified the diffusion kinetics and thermodynamic conditions, which in turn influenced the balance between face‐centered cubic (FCC) and body‐centered cubic (BCC) phases.
recalled_precedents.finding: Their work showed that appropriate heat treatment can suppress the formation of brittle ordered phases (such as the B2 phase) and promote a desirable mixture of ductile FCC and strengthening BCC phases, thereby optimizing mechanical properties.

recalled_precedents.approach: In their investigations, they modulated the cooling rates and subsequent thermal treatments of similar high-entropy systems. Rapid solidification techniques followed by controlled annealing were used as a strategy to steer phase transformations.
recalled_precedents.finding: They observed that precise control of the cooling and annealing schedule allowed the stabilization of targeted metastable phases, which led to improved microstructural uniformity and enhanced property performance.

recalled_precedents.approach: This study explored alternative processing routes such as mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering. These non-equilibrium processing methods were used to deliberately influence phase formation and transformation in HEAs related to the Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni system.
recalled_precedents.finding: Their results indicated that such processing techniques effectively produced fine-scale microstructures and stabilized phases that are otherwise difficult to obtain through conventional melting, thus opening the door to tailoring mechanical behavior via controlled phase evolution.
